title: QB4_E taught 'IACS UR Z7: ESP for Bulk Carriers and Tankers'. UR Z7 is Hull Classification Surveys and applies to all self-propelled vessels; the Enhanced Survey Programme is statutory under the 2011 ESP Code and SOLAS XI-1/2, and Z7's own section 1.1.3 routes the additional tanker and bulk-carrier hull requirements to the UR Z10 series
authorisation_source: Founder brief PRE-TRANCHE-4 PROPAGATION CLEANUP, sections 4-6, which names QB4_E as the third authorised residual, forbids substituting a guessed Z10 sub-number, and authorises a bounded same-defect propagation sweep.
candidate_claim: Not raised by a candidate. Carried into this pass by the Founder brief as a known false teaching.
candidate_verdict: UPHELD, AND VERIFIED AT THE INSTRUMENT RATHER THAN FROM THE BRIEF. The brief asserted both that Z7 is Hull Classification Surveys and that ESP belongs to the Z10 series. Both were checked against the held UR Z7 itself before anything was written.

authority.instrument: IACS Unified Requirement Z7 - Hull Classification Surveys, Rev.29 May 2022 / Corr.1 May 2024 (IACS Req. 1990/Rev.29 Corr.1 2024), clean text, 52 pages.
authority.acquisition_by_this_pass: NONE. UR Z7 was already held, hash-pinned and registered by the Tranche 3C custody repair earlier the same day. It was READ IN THIS PASS rather than assumed - the brief's instruction 'Do NOT treat Z7 as ESP after reading it' was taken to mean the document had to be opened, and it was.

operative_text.title_page: The document's contents page and running header read 'Z7 (cont'd) Hull Classification Surveys'. It is not an ESP instrument and its title says so.
operative_text.section_1_1_1: 'These requirements apply to all self-propelled vessels.' Z7 is therefore the BASELINE hull survey requirement for every ship, not a regime aimed at two ship types.
operative_text.section_1_1_3: 'For additional requirements for hull structure, piping systems and ballast tanks applicable to tankers, bulk carriers, chemical tankers, double hulled tankers, double side skin bulk carriers, general dry cargo ships and liquefied gas carriers, refer to Z10.1, Z10.2, Z10.3, Z10.4, Z10.5, Z7.1 and Z7.2 respectively.' This is Z7 itself routing the enhanced tanker and bulk-carrier hull requirements OUT of Z7 and INTO the Z10 series - the clearest possible refutation of the corrected claim, from the very document the claim cited.
operative_text.section_1_1_5: 'For additional requirements applicable to water level detectors fitted on single hold cargo ships, refer to UR Z7.1.' This is what UR Z7.1 actually is, and it disposes of the second, differently-numbered instance of the same defect found by the sweep.

authority.statutory_authority_for_esp: The Enhanced Survey Programme's mandatory status is STATUTORY, not class-derived: the International Code on the Enhanced Programme of Inspections during Surveys of Bulk Carriers and Oil Tankers, 2011 (ESP Code), IMO Assembly resolution A.1049(27), made mandatory through SOLAS Chapter XI-1, Regulation 2. This is not a new claim: it is already the corpus's own verified position at QB1_I#q1 (which additionally records that the ESP Code 'aligns closely with IACS UR Z10') and at meoclass1/oralnotes/miw-notes-mgmt-p21.html, whose verification note corrects an earlier 'ESP Code 2017' misnomer to exactly this citation. The correction therefore MOVES QB4_E onto the corpus's already-verified position rather than inventing one for it.
authority.why_no_exact_z10_sub_number_is_asserted: DELIBERATE, AND THE MOST IMPORTANT RESTRAINT IN THIS RECORD. The brief forbade replacing Z7 with a guessed Z10 sub-number. That prohibition proved to be load-bearing. Read strictly, Z7 section 1.1.3's 'respectively' maps tankers -> Z10.1 and bulk carriers -> Z10.2, which is the OPPOSITE of the widely-repeated secondary assumption that Z10.1 is bulk carriers and Z10.2 is oil tankers. Nothing held resolves which reading is right, and neither Z10.1 nor Z10.2 is in the repository. Neither card needs a sub-number: q9 teaches age-driven survey escalation and q12 teaches what a UR is. Both are therefore written to the generic 'UR Z10 series', which is exactly what Z7 section 1.1.3 supports and no more. No Z10 document was acquired, because acquiring one would not have been needed to write anything this record actually says.
authority.open_question_referred_forward: Which Z10 sub-number governs oil tankers and which governs bulk carriers is UNRESOLVED and is referred to GPT. It becomes live only if a future card needs a sub-number-level citation; it is not needed by anything now shipped.

cards.supersedes_note: q9 has never been pinned by any earlier correction or batch record. No ancestry is rewritten.
cards.rationale: The proposition the card is actually teaching was identified first, as the brief required: q9 answers 'Age norms for ships - age-related requirements and restrictions?' and its class limb teaches that survey scope escalates with age for tankers and bulk carriers. That proposition is SOUND; only its authority was wrong. So the escalation content, the 5/10/15-year brackets, the POOR-coating consequence, the MARPOL Annex I Reg 19/20 limb, the DGS Order 1 of 2026 limb and the commercial-vetting limb are all untouched. Four sites carried the false authority and all four now carry the true one: the 60-second answer, the sub-heading 'Classification and ESP (IACS UR Z7)', the Numbers/Regs line 'IACS UR Z7: ESP for Bulk Carriers and Tankers.' and the reg-box row 'IACS UR Z7 / ESP rules' (which had an EMPTY description, so the wrong code was the whole of its content). The Numbers/Regs line and the reg box additionally now state positively what UR Z7 IS, because a candidate who has memorised 'Z7 = ESP' needs the replacement fact, not just the absence of the old one.

cards.supersedes_note: q12 has never been pinned by any earlier correction or batch record.
cards.rationale: The same false attribution, in the same file, used three times as the WORKED EXAMPLE of what an IACS Unified Requirement is - in the 60-second answer, in the CE-relevance block, and in the reg box. That is worse than a stray citation: the card is teaching the concept 'UR' THROUGH this example, so the error is what the candidate is most likely to retain. All three now name UR Z7 as hull classification surveys and the Z10 series as the enhanced bulk-carrier / oil-tanker surveys. The UR E26/E27 cyber limb in the same sentence is correct and was not touched; the IACS membership list, the RMRS withdrawal and every other q12 proposition are outside this correction and unchanged.

propagation.sweep_definition: Bounded to the single adjudicated proposition - positive teaching that a UR Z7-series requirement IS the Enhanced Survey Programme. Every occurrence of 'Z7' in every candidate-facing HTML surface under meoclass1/ was extracted with context and intersected with ESP / 'Enhanced Survey' wording. Run before and after the edits. Separately, every occurrence of 'ESP' corpus-wide was read to find instances expressed WITHOUT the string 'Z7', which is how the simon-notes-p3 pair was found.

artefacts.digest_pin_note: An oralnotes page is not a q-card surface and carries no card digest, following the convention used for revision surfaces.
artefacts.found_by: The bounded section-6 sweep, NOT by the brief. The brief named QB4_E only. This page carried the identical defect under a DIFFERENT sub-number - 'mandatory under IACS UR Z7.1' - which is why it survived every prior pass that searched for the literal string 'Z7'.
detail: Prose: 'Enhanced Survey Programme - applicable to oil tankers and bulk carriers; mandatory under IACS UR Z7.1.' now cites SOLAS Reg XI-1/2 and the 2011 ESP Code for the mandatory status, points to the UR Z10 series for the class requirements, and states explicitly that neither Z7 nor Z7.1 is ESP. UR Z7.1's real subject - water level detectors on single-hold cargo ships - is given from Z7 section 1.1.5.

The paired reg box, which carried 'IACS UR Z7.1' as the reg CODE with the description '"IACS UR Z7.1 - Enhanced Survey Programme" - applies to oil tankers and bulk carriers >=500GT; verify exact UR number before quoting'. The hedge is NOT a saving qualifier and was treated as part of the defect: the wrong number was still the one printed in the code column, and the instruction to go and verify it was handed to the candidate. The number is now verified against the held UR Z7, so the hedge is discharged rather than carried forward. The >=500 GT figure was also split correctly - bulk carriers >=500 GT and oil tankers >=5,000 GT, per the corpus's own verified QB1_I#q1.
artefacts.sequencing_note: The reg box was MISSED by the first edit of this file and caught by the post-edit re-sweep, which is the reason the sweep is run after the edits and not only before them. A prose fix that leaves its paired reg box uncorrected produces a page that contradicts itself at the exact point a candidate looks for the citation.
